title: Psychrometric Studio project
description: A saved project. Stores states as the user *declared* them rather than as solved values, so that reopening at a different site pressure re-solves instead of carrying stale properties.

schemaVersion.description: Incremented on any breaking change to this format. Readers must refuse versions they do not understand rather than guessing.

airstreams.description: One or more airstreams. A single-AHU study has one; energy recovery, indirect evaporative cooling, and mixing with a distinct source all use two or more. First-class from the outset so it never needs retrofitting.

unitSystem.description: IP is primary. Calculations run natively in the selected system.

createdWith.description: Application and calculation-basis versions that produced the file. Stamped for traceability; never trusted for behaviour.

atmosphere.description: Site barometric pressure. Stored as its basis, not only its value, so a report can say where the number came from.

altitude.description: Site elevation, ft (IP) or m (SI). Required when basis is 'altitude'.

pressure.description: Barometric pressure in canonical units: psia (IP) or Pa (SI). Required when basis is 'explicit'.

stages.description: An ordered chain. Each stage takes the leaving state of the previous one.

airflow.description: Volumetric airflow, CFM (IP) or L/s (SI). Omit to inherit the upstream mass flow.

params.description: Process parameters, keyed by stage type. Validated by the process model rather than by this schema, so that adding a process type does not require a schema version bump.

couplings.description: References to other airstreams or stages. This is how a mixing box names its second stream, how a recovery device names the stream it exchanges with, and how a wrap-around coil's two legs find each other.

role.description: What the referenced stream is to this stage.

stageId.description: Optional. Names the specific stage whose leaving state is used; defaults to the referenced airstream's terminal state.

stateInput.description: A state as declared by the user. Which pair was entered is preserved, because re-solving at a new pressure must honour the original intent.

humidityRatioRange.description: Both ends of the humidity axis, canonical lb/lb or kg/kg. The view can be panned as well as zoomed, so the bottom of the axis is not always zero and storing only the top would lose the pan.

maxHumidityRatio.description: Superseded by humidityRatioRange. Still accepted on read, where it is taken as the top of an axis starting at zero.

comfortSettings.description: ASHRAE 55 inputs. Absent means no comfort overlay is drawn.

clothingWinter.description: Clothing insulation for the winter zone, clo. Named rather than positional: an array of two numbers does not say which end is which, and a reader that guesses wrong swaps the two zones silently.

clothing.description: Superseded by clothingWinter and clothingSummer. Still accepted on read as [winter, summer].

adaptiveIndoor.description: Indoor operative temperature assessed against the adaptive model, in the project's temperature units.

adaptivePrevailing.description: Prevailing mean outdoor temperature for the adaptive model, in the project's temperature units.

airSpeed.description: Average air speed, m/s. Above 0.2 the still-air PMV method does not apply; the elevated-air-speed cooling effect is out of scope for v1.

meanRadiantTemperatureOffset.description: MRT minus dry bulb, in the project's temperature units. Zero means MRT tracks dry bulb.

temperatureOffset.description: Horizontal shift applied to the comfort polygon. Zero in v1; reserved for the SET elevated-air-speed cooling effect so that adding it later is not a restructure.

weatherSettings.description: How the weather overlay was configured. The EPW file itself is deliberately NOT stored: it is roughly 1.5 MB of text that would dominate the project file, it is redistributable only under the source's own terms, and it is reproducible from the station identity below. On load the tool names the station and asks for the file again.

station.description: Enough to recognise the file that was used, and to tell the user they have opened the wrong one.

hours.description: Hours of the day included, 0-23. Empty means all.
